title: Kit pad level matching flattens drum dynamics and boosts long tails (crash +14 dB)
description: Found with examples/salamander-beat.apr (Salamander Drumkit, warp repitch one-shots). apricity explain shows each pad's whole clip level-matched (target about -20 dBFS RMS, see docs/concepts.md level matching; compile.rs ~906-933). Effects: (1) a crash with an 11.5 s tail gets +14 dB and dominates; drums track peaks +4.8 dBFS and crash +6.0 dBFS before the master limiter; (2) ghost, backbeat and kick end up equally loud, so kit dynamics are flattened. Options: measure level from the attack window (first N ms) for one-shot pads; or let a pad/clip opt out (keep recorded level, e.g. 'level as-recorded' or volume only); or match on peak. Needs Gherkin first, and a decision on whether it belongs in kit/pad vocabulary (coordinate with the vocabulary session). Repro: apricity explain examples/salamander-beat.apr (uncommitted example; fetch with apricity sources fetch salamander-drumkit, analyze with apricity_analyze.cli --no-notes).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed on develop: pads levelled together per source folder by their attacks (peak beat loudness). Salamander Beat: 8 pads at -3.4 dB (was +14 dB); crash peak before the limiter -11.4 dBFS (was +6.0).
